n4-licao-config.titulo: The bulletin board and the envelope: ConfigMap and Secret
n4-licao-config.enunciado:
The same image runs in different places (testing, production, the store in another city). Whatever changes from one place to another lives outside the image, in two objects:

  • ConfigMap: settings as text (COR: azul, a whole config file);
  • Secret: what must not leak (passwords, tokens). It stores the values in base64.

Three ways for the pod to use them

env:                         # 1. one key into one variable
- name: COR
  valueFrom:
    configMapKeyRef:           # (in a Secret: secretKeyRef)
      name: loja-config
      key: COR
envFrom:                     # 2. all the keys at once
- configMapRef:
    name: loja-config
volumes:                     # 3. each key becomes a file
- name: config
  configMap:
    name: loja-config

In the third way, the container mounts the volume with volumeMounts (name and mountPath) and finds one file per key in that folder. ConfigMap and Secret volumes are always read-only.

When the notice changes

Changed the ConfigMap? The mounted file follows along on its own (within a minute). The environment variable doesn’t: it’s read when the container starts. For the pods to see the new value: kubectl rollout restart deployment/NAME.

base64 is not encryption

kubectl get secret wifi -o jsonpath='{.data.senha}' | base64 -d shows the password to anyone who can read the Secret. What really protects it is who is allowed to read it (RBAC, in level 8) and etcd encryption.
n4-licao-config.vidaReal: The ConfigMap is the building’s bulletin board (pool hours, the color of the facade); the Secret is the sealed envelope with the gate code.
n4-licao-config.limite: The Kubernetes envelope isn’t a safe: the content is only base64, which anyone with access to the Secret can decode.

n4-licao-volumes.titulo: The work desk and the storage unit in the garage: volumes
n4-licao-volumes.enunciado:
A container’s filesystem is disposable: restart it, and whatever was written is gone. To keep data, you mount a volume:

  • emptyDir: an empty folder born with the pod. The pod’s containers share the folder, and it survives a container restart, but goes away with the pod.
  • PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC): the request for a disk (“I want 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce”). The real disk is the PersistentVolume (PV), and it exists outside the pods: the pod goes away, the PV stays.
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: dados
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]   # one node at a time
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi

And in the pod: volumes: [{ name: dados, persistentVolumeClaim: { claimName: dados } }] plus the volumeMounts in the container.

Who creates the disk: the StorageClass

Nobody has to create a PV by hand: the StorageClass knows how to create disks. In this cluster (as in kind), the default class is standard, from the rancher.io/local-path provisioner, with WaitForFirstConsumer: the PVC stays Pending until a pod uses it, and then the disk is created on that pod’s node. See it with kubectl get sc, kubectl get pvc and kubectl get pv.

PVC stuck in Pending with a pod using it? kubectl describe pvc NAME tells you why (for example, a StorageClass that doesn’t exist).
n4-licao-volumes.vidaReal: The emptyDir is the apartment’s work desk: the residents share it, but it leaves with the move. The PVC is the request for a storage unit in the garage: the unit is still there when the resident moves out.
n4-licao-volumes.limite: The local-path storage unit (kind’s disk) lives on a single node: a pod that needs it always goes to that node.

n4-licao-statefulset.enunciado:
Databases and queues need identity: each replica keeps its own data, and the others need to find it by name. The StatefulSet gives you that:

  • fixed, numbered names: db-0, db-1, db-2 (deleted db-1? another db-1 comes back);
  • creation in order: db-1 is only created once db-0 is ready; when scaling down, the highest number leaves first;
  • one disk per pod, through volumeClaimTemplates: dados-db-0, dados-db-1... The PVCs stay when the StatefulSet scales down (the data waits for the pods to come back);
  • one DNS name per pod, with a headless Service (clusterIP: None) named in serviceName: db-0.db.default.svc.cluster.local.
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 3
  ...
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: dados
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi

Hint: busybox’s nslookup doesn’t complete names that contain a dot. Use the full name: nslookup db-0.db.default.svc.cluster.local.
n4-licao-statefulset.vidaReal: In a Deployment, the residents are interchangeable (any of them can answer). In a StatefulSet, each apartment has a fixed number (101, 102...) and its own storage unit, even when the resident is replaced.
n4-licao-statefulset.limite: A fixed number isn’t a fixed address: pod db-0 may come back with a different IP. What stays is the DNS name and the disk.

n4-cor-da-vitrine.titulo: The color of the shop window
n4-cor-da-vitrine.enunciado: The store shows the color of its shop window in the JSON response (the cor field), read from the COR variable. Create the ConfigMap loja-config with COR: verde and make the store’s Deployment read the COR variable from it.
n4-cor-da-vitrine.dica: env: - name: COR, valueFrom: configMapKeyRef: name and key.
n4-cor-da-vitrine.vidaReal: Pinning “the facade is green” on the bulletin board: whoever paints it reads the board, instead of each painter deciding.
n4-cor-da-vitrine.limite: The store only reads the board when it opens: change the notice afterwards and it keeps the old color until it reopens (the rollout restart).
n4-cor-da-vitrine.comoSaber: kubectl port-forward svc/loja 8080:80 and then curl localhost:8080: the response has "cor":"verde".

n4-envfrom.enunciado: loja-config already has two keys (COR and PROMOCAO). Instead of one variable per key, bring all the keys into the store’s container with envFrom.
n4-envfrom.dica: envFrom: - configMapRef: name: loja-config (at the same level as image, inside the container).
n4-envfrom.vidaReal: Instead of copying the notices one by one, the store takes a photo of the whole board.
n4-envfrom.limite: A new key on the board only gets in when the pod restarts. And since Kubernetes 1.34 even a key like “cor-da-porta” becomes a variable, but the shell can’t read a name with a hyphen ($cor-da-porta doesn’t work): prefer COR_DA_PORTA.

n4-avisos-pelo-terminal.enunciado: Create, from the terminal only, the ConfigMap avisos with two keys: COR=azul and HORARIO=8h-18h.
n4-avisos-pelo-terminal.dica: kubectl create configmap NAME --from-literal=KEY=value (one --from-literal per key).
n4-avisos-pelo-terminal.vidaReal: Dictating the notices to the management office instead of writing them down on paper.
n4-avisos-pelo-terminal.limite: Done from the terminal, the notice isn’t saved in any file: to recreate the cluster, you’d have to remember the command.
n4-avisos-pelo-terminal.comoSaber: kubectl describe configmap avisos shows both keys.

n4-senha-do-banco.enunciado: The postgres is in CrashLoopBackOff. Read the logs (kubectl logs deploy/banco): it requires the POSTGRES_PASSWORD variable. Create the Secret banco-senha with the key senha and pass the value to the variable with secretKeyRef (no writing the password in the Deployment).
n4-senha-do-banco.dica: In the Secret, stringData accepts plain text (the server converts it to base64). In the container: env, valueFrom, secretKeyRef.
n4-senha-do-banco.vidaReal: The new building manager can’t open the safe without the combination, and the combination comes in a sealed envelope, not painted on the door.
n4-senha-do-banco.limite: The envelope (Secret) only hides it from whoever isn’t allowed to read Secrets; whoever is allowed reads it in plain text.
n4-senha-do-banco.comoSaber: kubectl get pods: the database ends up 1/1 Running.

msgs.1: the Secret banco-senha has the key senha

testes.descricao: the password comes from the Secret

n4-envelope-aberto.enunciado: The Secret wifi holds the Wi-Fi password for the construction site. Find out the password from the terminal.
n4-envelope-aberto.dica: kubectl get secret wifi -o jsonpath='{.data.senha}' shows the value in base64; finish with | base64 -d.
n4-envelope-aberto.vidaReal: The “sealed” envelope is only held shut with paper glue: anyone holding the envelope can read the password.
n4-envelope-aberto.limite: Here you’re allowed to read Secrets. In a well-configured cluster, most people aren’t.

msgs.0: you decoded the base64 in the terminal

n4-chave-errada.titulo: The wrong key in the envelope
n4-chave-errada.enunciado: The database won’t get out of CreateContainerConfigError. Find out why with kubectl describe pod NAME (in the Events) and check the Secret’s keys with kubectl describe secret banco-senha. Fix the Deployment.
n4-chave-errada.dica: The secretKeyRef must name a key that exists in the Secret.
n4-chave-errada.vidaReal: The note says “the combination is in the envelope, on the password line”, but the envelope only has a “senha” line.
n4-chave-errada.limite: The kubelet doesn’t guess: a key that doesn’t exist blocks the container (unless the reference is optional).

n4-vitrine-volume.enunciado: The ConfigMap vitrine-html has an index.html with the sale. Mount this ConfigMap as a volume at /usr/share/nginx/html in the shop window’s container, so nginx shows the sale instead of the default page.
n4-vitrine-volume.dica: Two places: spec.template.spec.volumes (the configMap volume) and volumeMounts in the container (name and mountPath).
n4-vitrine-volume.vidaReal: Instead of repainting the shop window, the store hangs the poster that came from the bulletin board.
n4-vitrine-volume.limite: The poster is read-only: inside the pod, nobody writes on it. To change it, you change the ConfigMap.
n4-vitrine-volume.comoSaber: From inside a shop window pod: kubectl exec deploy/vitrine -- curl -s localhost shows the sale.

testes.descricao: the shop window shows the sale
every shop window pod shows it

n4-aviso-novo.titulo: The notice changed, the store didn’t
n4-aviso-novo.enunciado: The store reads COR from the ConfigMap loja-config, which says azul. Change the notice to verde (the file is in the editor), apply it and make the store start showing "cor":"verde".
n4-aviso-novo.dica: Applying the ConfigMap isn’t enough: variables are read when the container starts. kubectl rollout restart deployment/loja.
n4-aviso-novo.vidaReal: They changed the notice on the board, but the store only reads the board when it opens. Close and open again (without leaving the customers out on the street).
n4-aviso-novo.limite: If the ConfigMap were mounted as a file, the file would change on its own; the environment variable, never.

testes.descricao: the store shows the new notice

n4-mesa-compartilhada.enunciado: The pod placa has two containers: pintor (the painter) writes the sign to /html/index.html and nginx serves /usr/share/nginx/html. Right now the painter can’t even write (see kubectl logs placa -c pintor). Add an emptyDir volume mounted on both folders, so nginx serves the sign the painter makes.
n4-mesa-compartilhada.dica: One emptyDir volume in spec.volumes and one volumeMounts in each container (different folders, the same volume). A pod can’t change after it’s created: kubectl delete pod placa and apply again.
n4-mesa-compartilhada.vidaReal: The painter and the window dresser work in the same apartment, but each at their own desk: the painter paints the sign and the window dresser never sees it.
n4-mesa-compartilhada.limite: The desk (emptyDir) belongs to the apartment (the pod): new pod, and it starts out empty.
n4-mesa-compartilhada.comoSaber: kubectl exec placa -c nginx -- curl -s localhost shows “Placa atualizada” (sign updated).

n4-box-na-garagem.titulo: A storage unit in the garage
n4-box-na-garagem.enunciado: The caderno (notebook) writes a line to /dados/notas.txt every time the pod starts, but the folder doesn’t even exist (see the logs). Create a PVC dados of 1Gi (ReadWriteOnce) and mount it at /dados. The notes must survive when the pod is replaced.
n4-box-na-garagem.dica: The PVC: accessModes and resources.requests.storage. In the Deployment: volumes with persistentVolumeClaim.claimName and volumeMounts.
n4-box-na-garagem.vidaReal: The notebook sits on the apartment’s desk and gets lost with every move. Rent a storage unit in the garage: the resident moves, the notebook stays.
n4-box-na-garagem.limite: This storage unit (local-path) lives on a single node; with a cloud disk, it could follow the pod to another node.
n4-box-na-garagem.comoSaber: kubectl get pvc shows Bound; delete the pod and watch kubectl exec deploy/caderno -- cat /dados/notas.txt grow.

testes.descricao: the notebook has its storage unit
the notes survive the pod being replaced

msgs.0: after the replacement, the file has the notes from both pods

n4-classe-que-nao-existe.enunciado: The galeria (gallery) has been Pending for ages. Investigate the PVC fotos (kubectl describe pvc fotos) and the disk classes (kubectl get sc). The PVC’s file is in the editor: fix it and recreate the request so the gallery comes up.
n4-classe-que-nao-existe.dica: A PVC can’t change its class: kubectl delete pvc fotos and then kubectl apply -f fotos.yaml (with the standard class, or no class at all, which uses the default).
n4-classe-que-nao-existe.vidaReal: Someone asked for a “climate-controlled” storage unit, but the condo only has regular ones. The request sits in a drawer, and the gallery waits at the door.
n4-classe-que-nao-existe.limite: The request can’t be amended: to change the type of storage unit, you cancel it and make a new one.

testes.descricao: the gallery comes up with a regular storage unit

n4-statefulset.enunciado: Set up the database db with 3 replicas of redis:7 in a StatefulSet: headless Service db (port 6379), serviceName: db and a 1Gi disk per pod (volumeClaimTemplates named dados, mounted at /data).
n4-statefulset.dica: It looks like a Deployment, with serviceName and volumeClaimTemplates on top. The selector must match the template’s labels.
n4-statefulset.vidaReal: Three numbered apartments, each with its own storage unit: number 1 is only handed over after number 0, and each resident always comes back to the same number.
n4-statefulset.limite: The StatefulSet knows nothing about databases: copying data between the replicas is the program’s job (redis, postgres...).
n4-statefulset.comoSaber: kubectl get pods -w shows db-0, then db-1, then db-2; kubectl get pvc shows dados-db-0, -1 and -2.

testes.descricao: the three apartments are ready, each with its own storage unit
db-1 comes back with the same name and the same data

msgs.1: the new db-1 found the old one’s file

n4-nome-fixo.enunciado: The StatefulSet db is up. From the pod cliente (busybox), find the IP of db-2 through DNS.
n4-nome-fixo.dica: kubectl exec cliente -- nslookup db-2.db.default.svc.cluster.local (busybox’s nslookup needs the full name).
n4-nome-fixo.vidaReal: To talk to apartment 2, the front gate looks up the list of residents by number, not by face.
n4-nome-fixo.limite: If db-2 is recreated, the name stays the same, but the IP may change: keep the name, not the IP.

n4-encolher.enunciado: Scale the StatefulSet db down to 1 replica, from the terminal. Then count: how many PVCs of db still exist?
n4-encolher.dica: kubectl scale statefulset db --replicas=1; then kubectl get pvc.
n4-encolher.vidaReal: In the off-season, apartments 2 and 1 close (in that order), but the storage units stay rented, with the stuff still inside.
n4-encolher.limite: Stored units cost money: with a cloud disk, a forgotten PVC stays on the bill.

testes.descricao: db shrank and the disks stayed

msgs.1: the PVC of db-2 is still there
